samples: This is a small command-line program that reads the numbers given as arguments, skips any argument that is not a valid number (printing a note about each one it skips), and then prints the mean, the median and the standard deviation of the remaining numbers, each rounded to three decimal places. The median averages the two middle values when the count is even, the standard deviation is the population version (it divides by the count, not by one less), and if no valid numbers were given each of the three lines says there is no data instead of failing. It needs only the console and the command-line arguments (no files, network or other side effects), and its three calculations are also public functions that other modules can reuse, each returning a number or nothing for an empty list.
